## The book manuscript

My book manuscript, *A Working Democracy: Progressivism and the Politics of
Work*, is under review. It's a study of Progressive Era intellectuals in the
United States, how they thought about work, and what they thought it meant for
democracy. One contribution the book makes is a new interpretation of
Progressivism as an ideology that centers work, an ideology that tried to make
space for cross-class solidarity. Along the way, it makes an argument for
including W.E.B. Du Bois among the Progressives, alongside Jane Addams, John
Dewey, and Charlotte Perkins Gilman. And it shows how figures like Herbert Croly
of *The New Republic* magazine helped to synthesize and popularize their ideas
in the period. I conclude by suggesting that there are aspects of the
Progressives' ideology of work that are worth keeping alive today, most of which
are rooted in the Progressive intellectuals' understanding of themselves as
workers.

## Cold War social science in the United States

I am also at work on an as-yet-unnamed project on the surprising
interdisciplinary exchanges during the Cold War in the United States. These
exchanges gave rise to what we now consider mainstream political science, and
gave birth to a new field that was at the time called (by its progenitors)
"policy sciences," and which we now know as the discipline of public policy. I
have presented work from this project to the Northeast Political Science
Association, the Association for Political Theory, and the Social Science
History Association. It's based in archival sources, and is therefore even more
slow-moving than my usual snail's pace. With support from the American
Philosophical Society and the Office of the Dean of Faculty, I am on leave
during the 2026–27 academic year so that I can get this project off the ground.
If you wish to follow the journey, then you can read my [public
notebook](notebook/index.qmd).
